      When Kent temperatures will reach nearly 20C again after grey and chilly spell

      Forecasters predict above average temperatures throughout the rest of the month

      Comments0
      News
      Sam Honey Multimedia Reporter
      15:53, 07 Oct 2026
      Listen to audio version of this article
      Sponsored by
      0:00 / 3:58
      Instaread

      Following an unusually warm start to October, new forecasts have revealed when temperatures will climb back towards the 20C mark after a spell of grey and chillier weather. While the working week began with widespread sunshine and above average temperatures for the majority of Kent, this has been replaced by gloomy skies and drizzle today (October 7).

      ‌

      Met Office forecasts describe showers spreading east through the afternoon, persisting along the coast into this evening. Temperatures, meanwhile, sit closer to what is typically expected in the autumn months, peaking at 15C at their warmest.

      ‌

      Skies in the south east are expected to largely clear overnight, though rain may linger over coastal towns, such as Dover and Folkestone, into the early morning. Any remaining showers will soon disperse to leave a generally fine start to Thursday (October 8), before overcast skies return in the late afternoon with a possibility for more rain and stronger winds overnight.

      ‌

      Once again, temperatures will sit around average, hitting 15C in the afternoon and sinking to 9C or 8C across Kent in the evening and overnight. It is from Friday (October 9) a return of the warmer weather is expected, with highs of 18C forecast for the majority of the county in the late afternoon.

      Watch as police chase down prolific Tunbridge Wells M&S thief who fled in an Audi

      Appeals renewed to identify two people found at foot of Dover cliffs 20 years apart

      However, the higher temperatures will be accompanied by further downpours, which could turn heavy at times, reaching up to 32mm/hr in some parts of Kent by the evening. Overnight, temperatures will again drop back down to the single digits, reaching as low as 8C in areas such as Ashford and Tunbridge Wells, making for a rather brisk start to the weekend.

      ‌
      Sign up to FREE email alerts from KentLive Daily newsletter

      We use your sign-up to provide content in ways you’ve consented to and improve our understanding of you. This may include adverts from us and third parties based on our knowledge of you. More info

      Weather patterns similar to those seen on Friday are forecast for Saturday (October 10), though afternoon temperatures will feel a little cooler at 16C for the majority of the region. Further showers are expected throughout the day, though these will be generally lighter and more isolated compared to those seen in the days prior.

      Sunday (October 11) is looking to be much drier overall with a mild afternoon, before the weather warms back up at the start of the following week. Met Office weather maps show widespread highs of 17C in Kent on Monday (October 12), climbing to 19C across the county on Tuesday afternoon (October 13) before dropping a little to 18C on Wednesday (October 14).

      From Thursday (October 15), temperatures will be a little closer to average, generally lingering around 15C at their warmest through the remainder of the week. Above average temperatures could return across the south east before the month is through, however.

      ‌

      The Met Office’s long range UK forecast for Monday, October 12 to Wednesday, October 21 describes: “Remaining changeable through the middle of October, as a series of low pressure systems run across the North Atlantic, often to the north and northwest of the UK, bringing occasional bands of rain and strong winds, but interspersed with brighter and more showery conditions. Rain will be most prevalent across hills in the west and especially northwest, where above average rainfall is likely through this period.

      “Longer drier interludes are more favoured in sheltered southern and eastern parts, but even here it is likely to be wetter than during recent weeks. Whilst brief cooler interludes are possible, temperatures are likely to be a little above average in many areas for the period as a whole, potentially quite warm in parts of the southeast early in the period.”

      Article continues below

      Changeable weather is expected across the UK for the remainder of October and start of November, with showers and longer spells of rain likely at times. While occasional colder interludes are possible, temperatures are expected to be near or a little above average for the period as a whole.
